features.title: Verified 373 seating and surcharge-train handling
features.behavior: 373-series (F) formations are classified as rotating reclining seats using the cited Tokaido Shizuoka formation list. Services carry JR Central's train type; limited expresses and Home Liners are labeled as needing an extra ticket on cards and featured legs, and complete-route planning never uses them as feeder or onward trains.
in_scope: Evidence-backed F formation metadata with a distinct rotating-reclining category
Optional trainType parsed from the existing JR Central feed and validated
Localized surcharge labels and connection-planning exclusion
out_of_scope: Fare calculation or per-section Home Liner boarding rules
Rewriting immutable archived bundles that predate trainType

verification.expected: Adapter, validation, classification, planner exclusion, localized UI, build, and smoke pass; an isolated live refresh emits trainType for corridor services.

evidence.result: Passed 59 Python tests, static/archive/model validation, 79 frontend tests, production build, and preview smoke for 30 daily bundles plus the formation model. The planner-exclusion regression failed when the exclusion was disabled. An isolated live refresh from the existing sources validated 434 October 27 services with train types (397 local, 20 limited express, 15 Home Liner, 2 rapid), and headless Chromium showed a labeled Home Liner with rotating reclining seats.

features.title: Archive-based predictions for unknown formations
features.behavior: When a displayed segment's formation is unknown because one or more operating diagrams lack a current assignment, passengers see a separately labeled cross-seat probability estimated from how often each diagram ran with each formation in the 30-day archive. Confirmed seat status, unknown status, and result filters are unchanged.
in_scope: Deterministic per-diagram formation-frequency model generated from the validated archive
Localized prediction display on result cards and itinerary legs
out_of_scope: Predicting services with no operating diagram (no training labels exist)
Classifying unverified families such as F (373 series) without seating evidence
Using predictions to hide or rank results

verification.expected: Model generation, validation, archive consistency, prediction logic, localized UI, build, and production smoke including formation-model.json pass.

evidence.result: Passed 57 Python tests, static/archive validation with an exact archive-consistency check of formation-model.json, 74 frontend tests, production build, and preview smoke for all 30 daily bundles plus the model. A rolling Git-history backtest (63 dates, 12067 known segment-days) scored 87.6% cross/no-cross accuracy with Brier 0.088; likely-cross labels were cross 92% of the time and likely-longitudinal 7%. Headless Chromium showed labeled live estimates on mobile cards and itinerary legs.

The push-triggered Pages workflow passed change detection, full verification, build, and deployment. The deployed data/formation-model.json matched the committed model (30 training dates, 83 diagrams).

features.title: Reliable automated data refresh and deployment checks
features.behavior: Scheduled refreshes preserve validated snapshots when source dates are unpublished, retry temporary network and push failures, and verify routing without assuming a changing daily itinerary is fixed.

verification.expected: Unavailable-source preservation, bounded retries, immutable route regression, the unchanged 1.5-second performance budget, archive validation, build, and production smoke pass.

evidence.result: Passed 50 Python tests, static/archive validation, 64 frontend tests, production build, and preview smoke for all 30 daily bundles. Preserved every saved JSON byte for unpublished dates, rejected malformed/partial current data and exhausted retries, tested push retries and unchanged-data deployment gating, preserved the exact 763M regression on four immutable September 9 services, and kept the 1.5-second bulk-planning budget including planner construction. Parsed both workflow YAML files and checked job dependencies. An isolated live October 2 refresh validated 416 JR Central services and 61 formation assignments without changing public/data.

Both Pages workflows passed 50 Python tests, static/archive validation, 64 frontend tests, production build, smoke for 30 daily bundles, and deployment. The live manually dispatched updater passed every step and pushed validated October 2 data with 416 services and 65 assignments, preserving the archive. The changed-data workflow gate correctly allowed the follow-up deployment.

features.title: Historical schedules and availability estimates
features.behavior: Passengers can browse 30 days of available snapshots, automatically view the latest past date, and see yesterday-based release estimates or the next scheduled check.

verification.expected: History publication, date selection, availability messages, existing routing, build, and static archive smoke pass.

evidence.repository_state: working tree based on 25fbadf; backfill from origin/main at e24ee78
evidence.result: Passed 27 Python tests, archive and static-data validation, 64 frontend tests, production build, and preview smoke for all 15 daily bundles. Recovered August 27–September 8 from validated same-commit pairs in remote history, preserving existing archives. Repeated backfill recovered zero dates. The selector exposes the full 30-day window and labels unavailable dates; scheduled updates retain the rolling window and backfill missing recorded dates.

features.title: Route-overlap-inclusive search
features.behavior: A passenger sees every upcoming same-direction train that operates over at least one segment of the selected corridor, classified as direct, first leg, or intermediate overlap without implying an unverified connection.
in_scope: Usable overlap display and connection-feasibility disclosure

verification.expected: Domain and UI tests cover all three route classes and one-station touches, then the production build and smoke checks pass.

evidence.result: Passed: 13 Python tests, static-data validation, 22 frontend tests covering all route classes, segment-only overlap, both directions, and departure-only ordering, then production build and smoke.

features.notes: Search remains globally sorted by the departure time at the start of each displayed usable segment.

features.title: Consolidated Shizuoka operation source
features.behavior: Current diagram assignments are read from the Tokaido Line Shizuoka Area Operation Information site's dated JSON mirror, while exact unique planned families provide a clearly disclosed fallback without overriding JR Central times.
in_scope: Unique U and F planned-family metadata from operation CSV assets
Current-over-planned precedence with no partial-source mixing
out_of_scope: Replacing JR Central station times with operation-table times

verification.expected: The adapter, conservative planned fallback, disclosure UI, static snapshots, and all existing checks pass without a direct Yulog request.

evidence.command: python3 -m scripts.update_data --source tokaido-shizuoka --operation-revision 202603 && npm run verify
evidence.result: Generated 433 JR Central services with 409 operation mappings, 161 segments carrying exact planned metadata, and 48 current assignments; verified JR time precedence for 1420M, omission of mixed planned data for 1422M, 16 Python tests, validation, 29 frontend tests, build, and production smoke.

features.notes: The target site states that its current-assignment display is populated with Yulog-provided data, so inherited provenance remains documented. The legacy yulog CLI value is only a deprecated alias for the Tokaido Shizuoka adapter.

features.title: Cross-seat-focused indirect results
features.behavior: Direct trains remain visible, while first-leg and intermediate-overlap trains are hidden only when their formation at the displayed overlap start is confirmed as all-longitudinal.
in_scope: Known and possible cross-seat indirect results
out_of_scope: Hiding unknown formations that may contain cross seats

verification.expected: Confirmed longitudinal first-leg and intermediate results are hidden, possible-cross and direct results remain visible, and all repository checks pass.

evidence.result: Passed 16 Python tests, static-data validation, and 35 frontend tests covering direct longitudinal preservation, confirmed-longitudinal filtering for both indirect route types, known cross seats, possible cross seats, production build, and preview smoke.

features.notes: Unknown and unverified formations count as possible cross-seat trains because the available data does not rule cross seating out.

features.title: Fastest complete itinerary for indirect results
features.behavior: Each displayed first-leg and intermediate-overlap result has an earliest-arrival scheduled itinerary from the selected origin to destination that includes the displayed train; indirect overlaps without a complete itinerary are hidden.
in_scope: Featured boarding at the formation-qualified overlap start
Omission of indirect overlaps without a complete scheduled itinerary
Disclosure that physical transfer feasibility is not modeled
out_of_scope: Backtracking or travel outside the Toyohashi–Atami corridor

verification.expected: Planner and UI tests cover first-leg, intermediate, missed-connection, earliest-arrival, and no-complete-route behavior before build and smoke pass.

evidence.result: Passed 16 Python tests, static-data validation, and 42 frontend tests covering constrained earliest arrival, feeder and onward legs, early transfer, missed featured boarding, reverse direction, indirect-result omission, localized UI itinerary, checked-in live routing, build, and production smoke.

features.notes: A scheduled connection is considered possible when the next train departs at or after arrival; platform movement and operational guarantees are disclosed as unmodeled.

features.title: Per-leg seating and result filters
features.behavior: Transfer itineraries disclose the formation and seat category of every leg, and passengers can configure direct longitudinal, direct unknown, indirect unknown, and minimum featured-ride visibility.
in_scope: Formation-at-boarding classification for every itinerary leg
Optional minimum scheduled minutes aboard the featured indirect train
out_of_scope: Filtering individual feeder or onward legs by seat type
Persisting filter settings across browser sessions

verification.expected: Domain and UI tests cover every visibility category, featured-ride duration, per-leg seating, build, and production smoke.

evidence.result: Passed 16 Python tests, static-data validation, and 44 frontend tests covering the four visibility settings, minimum featured-ride boundary, filter controls, per-leg longitudinal and cross-seat categories/formations, featured duration display, build, and production smoke.

features.notes: The minimum-duration input applies to scheduled time aboard the featured indirect train, not total itinerary duration. Visibility defaults preserve RADAR-003 behavior.

features.title: Robust constrained-journey ranking
features.behavior: Complete routes containing a featured train rank by earliest final arrival, then latest origin departure, then fewer transfers and shorter transfer waits without prematurely discarding feasible alternatives.
in_scope: Reverse-direction, overnight, dead-end, and early-alighting audit
out_of_scope: Minimum physical transfer times without platform data
Unconstrained fastest routes that omit the featured train

verification.expected: Adversarial and checked-in timetable regressions pass with intuitive latest-feeder selection and all production checks.

evidence.result: Passed 16 Python tests, static-data validation, and 55 frontend tests including the exact 763M feeder regression, exhaustive indirect Atami-to-Toyohashi consistency and direct-feeder dominance checks, adversarial ranking ties, reverse direction, overnight routing, build, and production smoke.

features.notes: The planner retains Pareto-safe feeder and onward alternatives. For 763M at Mishima it selects 1425M (Atami 08:47) instead of the unnecessarily early 423M (06:18), while preserving earliest final-arrival priority.

features.title: Responsive bulk indirect-route search
features.behavior: Long-corridor searches reuse timetable routing work so an Atami-to-Toyohashi 06:00 query does not block the interface for seconds.
in_scope: Early omission of formation-filtered indirect candidates
out_of_scope: Relaxing route correctness or formation filtering

verification.expected: The exact long-corridor query completes within its regression budget while all route-ranking and production checks pass.

evidence.result: Passed 16 Python tests, static-data validation, 55 frontend tests, production build, and preview smoke. The checked-in Atami-to-Toyohashi 06:00 audit planned all 202 indirect candidates in about 0.33 seconds and passed its 1.5-second regression budget, down from about 2.4 seconds.

features.notes: The planner caches Pareto-safe feeder and destination-bound onward profiles for each query. The UI also removes confirmed-longitudinal and disabled-unknown candidates before complete-route and per-leg formation work.
